argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0305c: meeting "c" (conceptual design) of series SY0305.

PROJECT
The team is designing a library self-checkout kiosk.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Industrial Designer (ID)  Priya  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Tomasz  present
C  Project Manager (PM)  Helen  present
D  User Interface designer (UI)  Kofi  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0305a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, noted that the industrial designer was absent because of a supplier visit, and had the marketing expert and user interface designer introduce themselves. The project manager presented the brief: a stand-alone self-checkout kiosk for medium-sized public libraries, to be original, trendy and user-friendly, sold at 3,500 euros per unit with a maximum production cost of 1,400 euros and a target of about 4,000 units in two years. The team discussed first ideas: the marketing expert stressed desk queues and the need to process a stack of books at once, which the user interface designer linked to RFID, although some libraries still use barcodes. The marketing expert raised accessibility for older users, children and wheelchair users, and the idea of matching library branding, possibly with a removable printable front panel. The user interface designer declared the kiosk would be touchscreen only, but this was questioned and the project manager deferred it to the next meeting. The project manager closed by assigning individual tasks for the functional design meeting, including the working design for the absent industrial designer.
  decisions: The kiosk must be able to process a stack of books at once rather than one book at a time. Accessibility (kiosk height, text size, suitability for older users, children and wheelchair users) will be treated as a requirement.
  actions: The industrial designer (absent) is to work on the working design: hardware components such as barcode scanner versus RFID pad, screen and casing, costed against the 1,400 euro limit. The project manager will email the industrial designer the notes and her assignment. The user interface designer will do the technical functions design, sketching the borrow and return flows. The marketing expert will research user requirements from library users and staff, including talking to the Wilson Street branch, and roughly check competitor pricing. The project manager will send out the minutes.
  problems: Whether to support RFID only or also include a barcode scanner is unresolved; RFID-only would exclude libraries still using barcodes, while adding a scanner raises cost and complexity. The user interface designer's claim that the kiosk will be touchscreen only with no physical buttons was not agreed and was deferred to the next meeting. The 1,400 euro production cost limit, including screen, scanner and casing, is considered tight.
  action item SY0305a.ai1: Working design: investigate hardware components (barcode scanner vs RFID pad, screen, casing, possible removable front panel) and their cost against the 1,400 euro limit (owner A, active)
  action item SY0305a.ai2: Email the absent industrial designer the meeting notes and her assignment (owner C, active)
  action item SY0305a.ai3: Technical functions design: define what the kiosk must do and sketch the borrow and return flows (owner D, active)
  action item SY0305a.ai4: User requirements: find out what library users and staff need, including talking to the Wilson Street branch (owner B, active)
  action item SY0305a.ai5: Roughly check what competitors charge for library self-checkout kiosks (owner B, active)
  action item SY0305a.ai6: Send out the meeting minutes (owner C, active)
  fact (absence): Priya (A), the industrial designer, was absent from the kickoff meeting because she was on a full-day supplier visit in Eindhoven.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): Kofi (D) declared that the kiosk would be touchscreen only with no keypad or physical buttons and called it decided; Tomasz questioned PIN entry, nobody agreed, and Helen deferred it to the next meeting.

[SY0305b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting, noted that the marketing expert was absent because he was interviewing staff at the Wilson Street branch, and confirmed that the industrial designer had received her assignment by email. The industrial designer presented a rough component costing: RFID pad, touchscreen, PC board, receipt printer and a casing with a removable printable front panel came to about 1,100 euros, rising to about 1,185 euros once a barcode scanner and a PIN keypad were added, which is within the 1,400 euro limit. The team agreed to combine RFID stack processing with a small barcode scanner for libraries that have not switched to RFID. The user interface designer presented the borrow, return and account functions. A fine payment feature was proposed but rejected because a card payment terminal would push the cost over the limit. The touchscreen-only question deferred from the kickoff was settled. The project manager relayed the marketing expert's notes that older users struggle with touchscreens and that competitor kiosks sell for 4,000 to 6,000 euros, and the team agreed on a touchscreen with a physical keypad for PIN entry only. The project manager assigned the absent marketing expert a research task and closed the meeting with actions for next time.
  decisions: The kiosk will use an RFID pad for stack processing plus a small barcode scanner for libraries still on barcodes. Fine payment will not be included on the kiosk in this version. Users can view fines but must pay at the desk. The kiosk will use a touchscreen for all interaction plus a physical keypad for PIN entry only.
  actions: The industrial designer will get firm supplier quotes for all components, including the barcode scanner and PIN keypad, and will check the front panel price with the printing supplier. The user interface designer will produce mockups of the borrow and return screens, including a large text mode. The marketing expert (absent) is to find out roughly what share of libraries still use barcodes and whether libraries require patrons to use a PIN. The project manager assigned this task. The project manager will email the marketing expert his task and will send out the minutes.
  problems: Where returned books go after check-in is unresolved, because a return bin with a sorter would be a separate, expensive machine. Barcode-only libraries will have to scan books one at a time rather than processing a stack. The share of libraries still using barcodes and whether libraries use patron PINs are unknown until the marketing expert reports back. The cost figures are rough estimates pending firm supplier quotes, including the front panel price.
  action item SY0305b.ai1: Get firm supplier quotes for all hardware components including the barcode scanner and PIN keypad, and check the removable front panel price with the printing supplier (owner A, active)
  action item SY0305b.ai2: Produce mockups of the borrow and return screens, including a large text mode (owner D, active)
  action item SY0305b.ai3: Mock up a fine payment screen for the kiosk (owner D, dropped)
  action item SY0305b.ai4: Find out roughly what share of libraries still use barcodes and whether libraries require patrons to use a PIN (owner B, active)
  action item SY0305b.ai5: Email the absent marketing expert to tell him about his new task (owner C, active)
  action item SY0305b.ai6: Send out the meeting minutes (owner C, active)
  fact (absence): Tomasz (B), the marketing expert, was absent from the functional design meeting because he was at the Wilson Street branch interviewing staff.
  fact (action_item_removed): Kofi (D) offered to mock up a fine payment screen and Helen (C) accepted, but later in the meeting Helen cancelled the task after fine payment was ruled out.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): Kofi (D) again argued for a touchscreen-only kiosk with no buttons, but the team instead chose a touchscreen with a PIN keypad.
  fact (plan_change): The touchscreen-only question deferred at the kickoff was resolved in favour of a touchscreen plus a physical PIN keypad, for accessibility.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F3_UNAGREED_DECISION [F3]: Someone raises a proposal as if it were a decision, but no one agrees to it and the meeting moves on without settling it. Record an F3 fact of type unagreed_proposal with agreed false. It must not appear in summary.decisions.
  Required gold labels: summary, qa_facts, edge_cases.
- F3_ACTION_REMOVED [F3]: An action item is created and later in the same meeting explicitly removed or cancelled. The action item has status dropped. Record an F3 fact of type action_item_removed linked to it.
  Required gold labels: action_items, qa_facts, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
